{span 04 a801 23 08}Body and soul bound to the weapon!
A mainstay melee attacker adept with a wide variety of weapons. Jack-of-all-trades, master of none{if 02}... As true in undeath as it was in life{/if}.
A mainstay ranged attacker adept with bow and crossbow, though their accuracy drops sharply in bad weather{if 02}... Which is no less true now that they're a zombie{/if}.
A magic-user boasting unrestricted access to all damage dealing spells{if 02}... Or did, once{/if}. Low defenses make them poor in close-quarters combat{if 02}―even now that they're a zombie{/if}.

A wielder of divine magic who mends wounds and cures various ailments{if 02}... Or was, once{/if}. Keep one in every battle party{if 02}. Of course, now that they're a zombie, you might think twice{/if}.
A well-rounded caster of attack and support spells who is also adept at sword and spear-play{if 02}... Or was, once{/if}. Able to move through water tiles{if 02}, even now that they're a zombie{/if}.
An excellent front-line warrior, able to use divine magic. Nothing halts the enemy's advance like a knight in their path. A strong defender and capable attacker{if 02}... At least, they were{/if}.

The howls of tormented spirits can be heard with every step of the terror knight's boots. Skilled in weakening enemy attacks and defense, they function as a wall to enemy advance{if 02}... Or, at least, they did{/if}.
A melee attacker entirely unconcerned with their own safety, the berserker boasts a strong attack, but subpar defense{if 02}. This is little changed now that they're a zombie{/if}.
A melee attacker and master of most bladed weaponry. Able to employ powerful war dances{if 02}, even now that they're a zombie{/if}.
A warrior with a special talent for slaying beasts and dragons{if 02}... At least, they used to be{/if}.
A nimble warrior who prefers hit-and-run tactics to an open fight. Their attacks with double weapons can be vicious{if 02}... At least, they used to be{/if}.
A {if 02}former {/if}master at relieving enemies of their treasured goods and laying traps to snare the unwary.

The fusilier can wield all of the powerful ranged weapons that give them their name. However, their eschewal of magic and all things supernatural has left them particularly susceptible to magic attacks{if 02}, and this is little changed now that they're a zombie{/if}.
The beast tamer is able to train beasts and dragons and unleash their hidden potential{if 02}... At least, they could, before they became a zombie{/if}.

Mage, fighter, explorer, these ardent scholars learn much of their trade from ancient writings. They are able to control golems and unleash their true potential{if 02}, a feat they can still perform even now that they're a zombie{/if}.
These masters of dark magic specialize in ranged combat and backing their minions from afar{if 02}―even now that they've become zombies themselves{/if}.
A mage possessing a ring of the dead, as well as a great deal of magical power{if 02}... Or once they did{/if}.
A mage-knight reincarnated through the use of an ensanguined rood, returning with powerful magics at their disposal{if 02}... At least, they were{/if}.
A {if 02}former {/if}heavily armored footsoldier, typically bearing sword and shield which they use{if 02}d{/if} to defend their clan upon the battlefield.
Destroyers upon the battlefield which display uncanny mobility despite their preference of heavy equipment{if 02}...before they turned into a zombie{/if}.
Adept at magic and a capable leader on the battlefield{if 02}―or at least they were{/if}. Wields magic powerful enough to impress even wizards{if 02}. This, at least, has not changed{/if}.

A minion of the cunning-folk {if 02}once {/if}able to attack and use utility spells to weaken foes and strengthen allies. Use them for defense, or as a decoy{if 02}―even now that they're a zombie{/if}.

This dragon, well-versed in the ways of the air, serves as a heavy unit on the battlefield. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}. Or at least, it used to{/if}.

This dragon, well-versed in the ways of the earth, serves as a heavy unit on the battlefield. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}. Or at least, it used to{/if}

This dragon, well-versed in the ways of lightning, serves as a heavy unit on the battlefield. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}. Or at least, it used to{/if}.

This dragon, well-versed in the ways of water, serves as a heavy unit on the battlefield. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}. Or at least, it used to{/if}.
This dragon, well-versed in the ways of fire, serves as a heavy unit on the battlefield. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}. Or at least, it used to{/if}.
This dragon, well-versed in the ways of ice, serves as a heavy unit on the battlefield. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}. Or at least, it used to{/if}.

This dragon is well-versed in the ways of the Light. Unlike most of its kin, it managed to suppress their savage nature and discover pleasure in protecting its allies{if 02}. Strangely, it still can{/if}.

This dragon is well-versed in the ways of the Dark. Unlike most of its kin, it revels in pain and suffering, often entering the fray with a barrage of powerful hexes{if 02}. And it is still able to{/if}.
A dragon with three heads. Its scales reduce damage taken while it deals death with tail and breath{if 02}―as it still does even now, as a zombie{/if}.
A behemoth fashioned of iron and stone. At first made and worshipped as a protector of a downtrodden people{if 02}. Few worship it now that it's a zombie{/if}.
This demon kin can fight with spell or blade and inflict a plethora of vile afflictions with breath and gaze{if 02}. And still can, now that it's a zombie{/if}.
Homunculi like this were usually created by powerful sages as retainers and stalwart guards of their abodes{if 02}. Not even death will end their vigil  {/if}.
A half-dragon champion that eschews martial training, instead relying on their vast strength and dragon magic{if 02}. And still does now that it's a zombie{/if}.
A monstrous lion with the head of an eagle and giant wings. Able to move with ease over rough terrain and changing elevations{if 02} even now, as a zombie{/if}.
A monstrous rooster with the scales and tail of a serpent. Its breath is enough to turn men to stone{if 02}―even now that it's a zombie{/if}.
A large monster that fights better in the water than on land―and, indeed, must be in water to employ special skills{if 02}. This holds true even now that it's a zombie{/if}.
An aggressive, violent giant, yet possessed of intellect enough to wield magic{if 02}―even now that it's a zombie{/if}.
{span 10 0a03 27 08}Title given by the Order of Philaha to those it deems worthy of carrying on the mantle of Valerian rule. Their power is largely a factor of their past achievements.
{span 10 3a03 2e 08}A wandering warrior adept in the use of a wide range of martial skills. Particularly good at taking out specific targets, rangers perform well in all manner of situations.
{span 0a ae02 31 08}A venerated cleric well-versed in matters of the spirit. Noted for their ability to use offensive divine magic.
{span 0e 9403 18 08}An evil priest who uses the power gained through their devotions to acquire a mastery of dark magic. Some are also surprisingly skilled in swordplay.
{span 10 ba03 32 08}Only one deemed to be the rightful heir to the Valerian Kingdom may become princess. The Princess serves as a mage-knight on the front lines to fight for peace in her kingdom.
{span 0a 5c02 26 08}A knight among knights, serving the king himself. Able to channel divine power through their blades.
{span 0a 5802 23 08}A master magus who draws upon the power of the stars to work their magic. Also a skilled diviner.
A winged warrior with a light step on the battlefield. Excellent at both melee and ranged attacks{if 02}... At least, they were{/if}.
{span 0c cc03 05 08}Only knights commander are granted the title of White Knight. In both defense and offense they are far superior to common knights.
{span 0a 0602 1c 08}An oracle serving the many gods of Valeria, shamans are adept at wielding elemental magic.
{span 06 7201 37 08}Don't you dare make the mistake of calling me a witch!
A traveling minstrel and singer of renown, able to perform enthralling songs and dances to encourage allies and dishearten enemies{if 02}―and still are able to, since becoming zombie{/if}.
{span 0c 2002 37 08}A pirate plying the Obero Sea, only those unaffiliated with any groups or orders are called by the name of buccaneer.
{span 10 d203 36 08}A warrior monk tasked with guarding the highest of the ecclesiarchy. They avail themselves of only the most basic of equipment, training their bodies to become harder than steel.
{span 10 d203 36 08}A warrior attuned to the primal forces of nature. They are able to freely channel those forces and shape them to create new life, or simply rain rock and fire upon their foes.
{span 10 d203 36 08}A master of the blade attuned to the energy of the universe. They are able to freely channel that force to perform feats of skill far beyond the grasp of a common soldier.
{span 10 d203 36 08}A scholar dedicated to the study of arcane constructs, animating them with unrivaled skill. As battlefield is the ultimate test of their creations, many are also capable warriors.
{span 10 d203 36 08}These hunters of men and monsters are the most at home in the wild. Often accompanied by tamed beasts, they possess a vast array of skills needed to track and subdue their prey.
{span 10 d203 36 08}A high-ranking knight of Lodis. Typically given command of 500 to 2000 troops, the Dark Knights Loslorien prefer to attack in smaller numbers (30 to 100) of highly trained elites.
{span 10 d203 36 08}A high-ranking knight of Lodis. Typically given command of 500 to 2000 troops, the Dark Knights Loslorien prefer to attack in smaller numbers (30 to 100) of highly trained elites.
{span 0e aa03 1e 08}The highest rank of knight in Lodis, given control of a knightly order. There are 16 such knights in Lodis, each thought to be worth 100 knights in battle.

{span 12 dc04 12 08}An arcane archer that carries the blessing of Nestharot, their arrows tearing the very firmament asunder to call forth the nature's calamity. A maiden is usually chosen, but there have been some exceptions.
{span 08 b602 18 08}An elite mercenary from Balboede, trained in the use of exotic weaponry and equipment.
{span 0a 8202 25 08}A fallen, demonic knight, sometimes seen leading the endless hordes of shambling, ravenous minions.
{span 10 a403 31 08}A fallen Dynast-King now corrupted by the Dark. More divine than human, the Dark Lord has forgotten much of his human life, and now only bears hatred and envy for the living.
{span 10 a403 31 08}A fallen Dynast-King now corrupted by the Dark. More divine than human, the Dark Lord has forgotten much of his human life, and now only bears hatred and envy for the living.
{span 0e d003 20 08}A ghast created by the merging of the Dark and a soul filled with hatred. This soul belonged to Dynast-King Dorgalua's arch-rival, King Rodrick of Brigantys.
A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Warrior.
A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of an Archer.

A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Berserker.

A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Ninja.

A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Beast Tamer.
A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Warlock.
A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Necromancer.

{span 12 8804 02 08}A magic-user whose command of a wide range of spells dwarfs the knowledge of a common wizard. Able to use their power without worshipping or forging a pact with any gods, demons, or spirits.
{span 0a 0202 1c 08}A killer-of-men for hire, will use any means at their disposal to claim their mark.
{span 0a 0202 1c 08}A fallen exarch who chose power over faith, attaining their rank by use of improper means.
{span 0a 0202 1c 08}A villager of Golyat, fleeing before the sudden attack of the Dark Knights and the Bakram.
{span 0e 7e03 18 08}One of the people driven from their village during Hierophant Balbatos's blood war. Many lay hidden in Lhazan Fortress following the Bakram invasion.
{span 0a 7002 23 08}This corpse of a man hanged for collaborating with the Bakram was animated by a dark necromancer.
{span 10 0e03 2b 08}The spirit of a dead sailor lingering in the depths of the Pirate's Graveyard. As long as they still yearn for something of their former lives, they will never be free.
{span 0a 1a02 21 08}A former swordmaster, skilled with the blade. Now fallen to killing men for a pittance of goth.
{span 06 6001 37 08}A dedicated assassin who revels in the taking of life.
{span 08 ae02 12 08}A dark mage that offered their very essence in exchange for limitless knowledge.
{span 08 1202 06 08}A fallen priest―an apostate who uses divine magic for personal gain.
{span 08 9a02 16 08}A mystic warrior fallen from grace, adept at infusing their blade with dark essence.
{span 0c 9e03 03 08}A knight who attained immortality through a pact with a demon. No light of reason shines in its eyes, only a lust for bloodshed.
{span 0a d602 2e 08}Ungodly means were used to fetch the soul of this knight from the Abyss who now animates this suit of armor.
{span 06 dc02 02 08}A savage raider that revels in removing heads from their bodies.
{span 08 0402 07 08}A born killer who thinks of taking lives as nothing more than a game.
{span 0c c603 05 08}An insane hunter of man or beast that kills not for honor, glory or gold. They live but for the sheer enjoyment of spilling blood.
{span 06 6601 36 08}A dweller in darkness, fed on the blood of the Abyss.
{span 08 3a02 10 08}A bandit skilled in inflicting so much pain, death feels like an afterthought.
{span 0a 1602 24 08}Snipers never hesitate to pull the trigger of their fusil on a man. In fact, they rather enjoy it.
{span 0a a402 2f 08}A savage master of dragon and beast who craves human flesh, often joining their pets in their gruesome feast.
{span 0c 9e03 06 08}An evil magus, conversant in all forms of spellcraft. Has the peculiar habit of taking men's skins to use as covers for spellbooks.
{span 08 1c02 07 08}A vile master of the dead, inspiring in equal parts fear and respect.
{span 10 e003 34 08}A dark winged creature, sometimes called the "Angel of Death." A raven rises when the Dark touches the corpse of a man who has passed on, having committed all seven deadly sins.
{span 06 9001 3a 08}A ruler of the underworld, wielding power without limits.
{span 08 f202 1e 08}The unearthly beauty of this winged stands in stark contrast to its brutally violent nature.
{span 0a f402 34 08}An ebon winged who fell onto the paths of darkness, the night crow will not cease battle until it has drawn blood.
{span 0a 3602 23 08}A variety of lizardman with blood-red skin. Its violence is remarkable, even toward its own kind.
{span 10 b003 2f 08}A wielder of ancient magic with a gaze that can turn those who draw too near to stone. Of the many tribes of gorgon, the Medusa, Stheno, and Euryale tribes are most famous.
{span 0a 7c02 29 08}Dark magic created this orc-human crossbreed. Superior in both strength and intellect to its forebears.
{span 08 ec02 19 08}A skeletal warrior and wielder of magic, fetched from the Abyss by means of necromancy.
{span 0a 3a02 20 08}A spirit warrior and wielder of powerful magic, fetched from the Abyss by means of necromancy.
{span 0c d403 08 08}A corrupted servant of the Divine, its once merely mischievous nature twisted into committing acts of horrible cruelty and suffering.
{span 0a 2a02 21 08}This nightmare flits nimbly through the air to dodge attacks. Also a wielder of powerful magic.
{span 0a 7802 29 08}This horrific creature lurched into life when the Dark settled upon a rotting pumpkin-headed scarecrow.

{span 1a 0405 1e 08}This dragon is named for the translucence of its steely scales. The material of its scales is second only to diamond in hardness, and the slight imperfections in its hide catch the light and sparkle like rubies and sapphires, adding to the ancient dragon's breathtaking appearance.
{span 0e 8e03 1a 08}Ebon scales cover the sinuous form of this wyrm of darkness. So dark are its scales that they absorb not only light, but the very will of men to fight.
{span 0e 6003 14 08}A dragon with many heads, spending much of its time in the water. Often takes the form of a beautiful woman to lure travellers to a watery grave.
{span 0c 8a03 01 08}Sometimes worshipped as a serpent god, the naga is nothing more than a vile, bloodthirsty monster intent on taking human life.
{span 0a d402 2d 08}A golem fashioned of damasc steel, the hardest variety of steel known to man. Immune to most melee attacks.
{span 0e 0803 0d 08}Some fiendish mage patched this golem together from a jumble of leftover body parts. Its bulbous form boils with hatred toward the living.
{span 0c 1202 36 08}A horse with the head of an eagle and giant wings. Able to fly with ease over rough terrain and changing elevations.
{span 0c e603 0d 08}The fabled immortal bird. Though legend says that any who drink the phoenix's blood will gain its immortality, this is likely just a myth.
{span 08 ca02 17 08}A giant demon-bird. It's said that the demons rode upon these during the Ogre Battle.
{span 0c 9a03 04 08}A serpentine desert-dweller with a gaze that can turn men to stone. When facing a basilisk, bring a shield, or don't come at all.
{span 08 8802 11 08}A dweller of the deep, the kraken can control water and summon squalls at will.
{span 0c 2802 34 08}An aquatic giant, the "Demon of the Sea." Can summon a great tempest to sweep its foes to the depths of the ocean.
{span 0c 0802 36 08}A one-eyed giant, adept in the use of elemental magic, just in case its inhuman strength isn't enough to do the job.
{span 0c e803 09 08}Member of an ancient race of giants. Sees out of only one eye, the other having been taken as punishment for turning against the gods.
{span 08 de02 19 08}An avatar of Vija, said to be the most martially adept of the Twelve Heavenly Generals.
{span 06 e802 03 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Enja, punisher of men's crimes.
{span 0a 7802 25 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Maitreya, who extends the hand of salvation to deserving mortals.
{span 08 7802 0f 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Ijana, who staves off disease and calamity.
{span 08 f802 19 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Chandra, who borrows the power of the moon in battle.
{span 08 5002 0b 08}An avatar of Vayu, said to be the wisest of the Twelve Heavenly Generals.
{span 08 6c02 0e 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Indra, who crushes the desires of mortals.
{span 0a 5402 22 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Rakshas, who brings destruction and devastation to this world.
{span 08 8202 0c 08}An avatar of Ahurama, known as an ogre among the Twelve Heavenly Generals.
{span 0c 3402 36 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Asurama, the great revealer, who protects and preserves the teachings of the gods.
{span 08 6202 0d 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Aditi, said to be a scourge upon mankind.
{span 08 f802 1a 08}An avatar of the Heavenly General Saranga, said to have shot a great demon with its bow.
{span 0a b802 2c 08}A guardian of the temple of Ashmedai. A normal person in appearance, her true form is shrouded in mystery.

{span 10 f803 38 08}A guardian of the temple of Ashmedai. It is unclear whether Blackmoor was once a human who reincarnated, or was a lich from the very beginning. His true form is shrouded in mystery.

{span 12 b404 0e 08}A monster, called the Sea Witch. Many are the men who have lost their lives at the bottom of the sea, lured into calamity by the dulcet tones of her voice. She feeds upon the souls of the men she kills.
{span 0c a003 06 08}The bird that pulls Hahnela's chariot across the sky. Worshipped as a divinity who calls the strong winds that usher in the spring.
{span 10 2203 23 08}A beastman said to have been created by Vaasa, Goddess of Earth, to serve her in eternity. Called the "Ravager" for his violence, Vaasa uses him for a watchdog.

{span 14 f804 23 08}The stormbeast, survived from the days of the Ogre Battle. Once a scourge upon mankind, Xolotl was captured by heroes who had received the protection of Nestharot, Goddess of Lightning. Now he serves as her temple guardian.

{span 14 ee04 26 08}Said to have been born from the tears Greuza, Goddess of Water, shed for her lost son, Tlaloc has been called a god of rain and of disasters. When the great winds blow, and the floods come, people say it is the work of Tlaloc.

{span 18 9e05 10 08}A creature of fire and a powerful elemental. Ifrit once wreaked havoc among the villages and towns of man, until Xoshonell, Goddess of Fire, caught him and trapped him within an urn. After many centuries, Ifrit repented, and now serves as Xoshonell's temple guardian.
{span 10 2c03 2d 08}A chimera with the body of a bird, shell of a turtle, and tail of a snake. It is said that Lyuneram, Goddess of Ice, turned a cruel king into this creature as punishment.

{span 0a 9a02 29 08}Krysaro: Though her guise might change and her power betray her, she knew her faith would never falter.

{span 0a f002 30 08}Phidoch South Curtain Wall: Not knowing they had been abandoned, the castle's defenders fought on to the last.
{span 08 3e02 0a 08}The Vanessan Way: Many fell here defending their land from the invaders.
{span 0a 7402 29 08}The Golborza Plain: Had they only fulfilled their duty, perhaps the ones that died here might yet live.
{span 08 4002 0c 08}Palace of the Dead: Even as one minion of the Dark falls, another is born.
{span 08 2402 06 08}Mount Weobry: Twice beaten, companions lost, where now will he flee?
{span 0a cc02 2d 08}Rhea Boum Aqueduct: Here the hunter cornered his prey, but Hope's star did not shine in these murky depths.
{span 08 ea02 19 08}Tzorious Field: A prince become slave, instrument of those who brought low his kingdom.
{span 08 fe02 1d 08}The Leupha Coast: The bracing sea air and glimmering sun lifted their battle-weary spirits.
{span 0a c002 2c 08}Twixt Heaven and Earth: He died fighting for vengeance, but was it the hand of god or man that judged him?
{span 0a 3802 1f 08}The Pirate's Graveyard: Though the journey seems at an end, the true reward waits just ahead.
{span 0a 2c02 22 08}The Arkhaiopolis of Rhime: A clever trap he laid, but he was too quick to underestimate his foe.

{span 14 ea04 29 08}Composer: Hitoshi Sakimoto / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Main Title (1:03)  "This is a piece that symbolizes the Ogre series. We layered instruments to add texture while still remaining faithful to the original orchestration." (Kudo)

{span 16 e804 3e 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Kimihiro Abe  Introduction (2:59)  "Iwata handled the chorus, while I added texture to the orchestration. The result was even more lavish than we expected, and I feel it really draws players into the story." (Abe)

{span 14 3604 13 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battle Party Formation (0:46)  "Warriors experience all manner of emotions as they prepare for battle. This piece aims to express these feelings." (Iwata)

{span 12 fc04 13 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Victory Screen (0:48)  "I aimed to recreate the joy and relief of victory, and, in the new parts, the excitement of collecting the spoils of war." (Iwata)
{span 0e 6403 13 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Retreat (0:30)  "This piece represents the sounds of soldiers fleeing from battle." (Iwata)
{span 0e 8003 12 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Game Over (0:17)  "I aimed to reflect the sadness and regret of death and defeat." (Iwata)

{span 1a b005 24 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  World Map (1:26)  "The game revolves around epic battles, so we used a more relaxed piece for the map screen. We extended the piece slightly, aiming for the feeling of reaching your destination at sunset after a long journey." (Iwata)

{span 1a f005 2a 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 3 (2:00)  "Nybeth commands the dead, meddling with souls in his quest for immortality. This can be thought of as his theme. A rhythm that portrays a resonating darkness has been added to the eerie scale of the original." (Iwata)

{span 14 ea04 27 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Yoshimi Kudo  Battlefield 5 (3:12)  "We added an ominously escalating flourish to the end of the original. I think the interplay between organ and orchestra is particularly poignant." (Kudo)

{span 14 c004 25 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Masaharu Iwata  Battlefield 7 (2:29)  "Battles must be fought to the bitter end. This mentality and the chaos of battle are portrayed in a piece slightly longer than the original." (Iwata)

{span 14 f804 29 08}Composer: Masaharu Iwata / Arranger: Noriyuki Kamikura  Battlefield 9 (1:47)  "We took care not to interfere with the atmosphere of the original. I think we captured the essence of Denam's will to battle on valiantly." (Kamikura)

{span 1a de47 02 10}  Press the {icon 12} button while viewing the world map or during battle to display the System Menu.
  Select the Data command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Options command to change settings such as the controls. In some cases the Retreat or Withdraw commands may also be available. Select these commands when you want to end the battle and return to the world map.

{span 18 e249 02 20}  Use the Save command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Load command to resume a saved game. You can save or load from the world map at any time by selecting the Data command from the System Menu.

- Quick Saves -
  Select Return to Title (Quick Save) to save your game during battle. This will suspend the battle so you can resume it at a later time. To resume your game, select Single Player and then Continue on the title screen. Note that quick saves are not erased after being loaded.

{span 1c 1645 2b 08}  A help message appears at the top of the screen for items selected by the cursor. To view help messages for items that cannot be selected, press the {icon 11} button. These select help messages can be useful when there is a large amount of information on screen, such as when viewing the party screen.

{span 1a c64d 37 50}  The game records your last 50 actions during battle. You can use the Chariot Tarot to call up this battle record and return to a previous point in a fight. When jumping to a previous point it is saved as a separate record, so you can compare results from before and after you retraced your steps.

- Using the Chariot Tarot -
  Press the {icon 9} button during the attack turn of one of your units or after interrupting the turns of others. You can also select Chariot Tarot from the System Menu.

- Same Actions, Same Results -
  If you perform the same actions after retracing your steps using the Chariot Tarot, the results will also be the same. You must perform different actions to change your fate in battle.

- Battle Log -
  Press the {icon 4} button while the Chariot Tarot is displayed to view a detailed log of each turn.

{span 1e 8453 28 68}  You can use the World Tarot to jump to certain points in previously completed areas of the story. These are called "anchor points."

- Moving Between Anchor Points -
  There are multiple anchor points in each chapter. You can view these by using the World Tarot command in the Warren Report. This time line is also used to select a specific anchor point to jump to.

- The Story is Reset -
  Your progress is saved as you pass each anchor point. When you jump to an anchor point, you resume playing from that point in the story. If you return to a point before an important decision is made, you can make that decision again.

- Your Party Remains Unchanged -
  Party details such as class levels, inventory, and war funds are retained when you jump to an anchor point. This is also true of units added to your party, though they may revert to guests not under your control depending on story developments. Even in these cases, they will always return to your party once their duties are complete.

- Lost Information -
  Each anchor point records your progress up to the point at which you passed it. For this reason, anything occurring after the selected anchor point will be lost.

{span 1a d84e 11 30}  Each anchor point records your progress up to the point you passed it. The status of each unit relating to the story is also saved. This means that when you use the World Tarot, you may experience some inconsistencies.

  For example, assume you had dismissed Canopus before passing Anchor Point B. If you later jump to Anchor Point B using the World Tarot, even if Canopus happens to be in your party, the story will continue on as if he had been dismissed. The same is true of the information in the Warren Report.

- Updating Anchor Point Data -
  Each time you pass an anchor point the data it contains is updated. Using the example above, if you jump to an anchor point before Canopus was dismissed, then pass Anchor Point B again without dismissing him, the Anchor Point B data will be updated to reflect his presence in your party.

{span 18 0e4d 0c 50}  You can move between various locations and customize your party on the world map.

- Main Menu -
  Press the {icon 3} button while the cursor is on your party to display the Main Menu for the world map. The Party and Warren Report commands can be used at any point on the map, while the Shop command only appears when your party is at a town or castle.

- Traversing the Map -
  To move to locations such as towns and castles, position the cursor over the desired destination and press the {icon 3} button. Events or battles may be triggered when you arrive at or pass through a map location.

- System Menu -
  Press the {icon 12} button to display the System Menu. Select the Data command to save your progress to the storage media, and the Options command to change settings such as the controls.

{span 16 3e47 22 20}  Some locations, such as castles, are comprised of multiple areas in which you may face several battles in a row. However, you can save your progress between battles. As on the world map, you can use Data on the System Menu to save.

- Saving Your Progress -
  You will not be able to leave a location until you have fought your way through the final stage. The use of multiple save games is strongly recommended.

{span 16 664a 26 38}  Before going into battle you must select the units to send into the fray. The units that take part in a battle are called the battle party. You can deploy up to 12 units in your battle party, but this number may be reduced on some battlefields.

- Terms of Victory -
  You can view the factors that will determine victory or defeat by selecting Terms of Victory. This information can be valuable when putting together your forces.

- Unit List -
  As with the Party command on the world map, you can use the Unit List command to change the equipment or skills of your units and examine the party's inventory.

{span 16 c04a 2f 38}  When battle starts, the unit with the lowest RT (Recovery Time) acts first. AT (Attack Turn) indicates the order that units take action.

- Attack Turn -
  You can issue commands such as Move and Act on a unit's attack turn. To issue a command, select a unit and press the {icon 3} button. Main Menu commands such as Move and Act will be displayed on the screen.

- Interrupt -
  You cannot issue commands during the attack turns of units not under your control. Press the {icon 4} button if you wish to confirm the status of units at times such as this. This interrupts the current unit's attack turn and allows you to use commands.

{span 16 8247 22 10}  Units can use the Move, Act, and Skills commands once each per attack turn. There is no restriction on the order in which these commands must be used. Skills can affect Move and Act commands, so a number of tactical options are available.
  Move commands can be reset and issued again up until the point another command is issued. This can be useful when you need to reposition a unit to be in range to attack.

{span 1c 3a57 23 78}  During battle the RT (Recovery Time) of units is compared to determine attack turn order, with units having lower RT taking their turn sooner. RT is determined by the base value for the unit, the weight of the equipment they carry, their class, and the actions they performed on their previous attack turn.

- Equipment Weight -
  Each piece of equipment displays a value for its weight. The greater its weight, the more it adds to the RT of units equipping it. It pays to take this into account when deciding which equipment to use.

- Class -
  Each class has a base RT value. The RT of similar units will vary depending on their class, affecting the order in which they act.

- Previous Attack Turn -
  Each action that is taken during an attack turn will have an impact on the RT for the next turn. This is determined by the distance covered with the Move command and the actions taken with Act and Skills commands. Equipment and spells also have RT values that are added to RT when they are used.

- Attack Turn List -
  When a unit is selected during battle, the row of units shown at the bottom of the screen indicates the expected AT order. To view the attack turn of all units in battle, press the {icon 4} button to display the Unit List, and use Sort Units to display them in order of attack turn.

  It is crucial to stay aware of which units will be acting next. Try to eliminate unnecessary actions to stay ahead of the enemy.

{span 18 e205 18 08}  Select Return to Title (Quick Save) to save your game during battle. This will suspend the battle so you can resume it at a later time. To resume your game, select Single Player and then Continue on the title screen. Note that quick saves are not erased after being loaded.

{span 16 404f 22 50}  Each unit has Life and HP that represent their physical endurance. Units whose HP falls to 0 during battle are incapacitated, and will lose a point of life if not aided. When a unit's life is exhausted, it is dead and can no longer be revived.

- Incapacitation -
  A counter appears above the heads of units incapacitated when their HP falls to 0. Each attack turn the counter decreases by 1, and if it reaches 0 that unit loses a life and is withdrawn from the battlefield.

- Withdrawn Units -
  Units withdrawn from the battlefield cannot take further actions during the current battle. However, they can take part in later battles as long as they have at least one point of life remaining.

- Death -
  Units that have no remaining life are deceased. Death is not reversible, so they will no longer be able to fight at your side. You can either Dismiss a deceased unit or Scavenge Skills to remove it from your party.

{span 14 804c 1f 40}  The movement range and elevation difference each unit can traverse vary depending on the movement type of its class. The skills assigned to a unit can also affect movement.
  The Move command can be reset and issued again up until the point another command is issued. This can be useful when you need to reposition a unit to be in range to attack.

- Crossing Gaps -
  Units can leap across gaps a single tile wide, but the other side of the gap must be of equal or lower elevation.

- Elevation Differences -
  The height a unit can jump up or down varies depending on its movement type. This can lead to situations where a unit can jump down to a lower spot but cannot climb back up, forcing a longer return route to be taken.

{span 1c 8a05 38 08}  The predicted outcome of an action is displayed when the cursor is placed on a target. For actions that cause damage, the expected damage dealt is shown on the left, and the chance of success is shown on the right. Check these values before executing a command to take the most effective course of action.

{span 16 a649 0f 48}  MP (Magic Points) are required to cast spells, and TP (Tactical Points) are required to use skills and finishing moves. MP and TP are reset to 0 at the beginning of each battle, meaning a unit must wait before using abilities that require MP or TP.

- Gaining MP -
  MP are accumulated gradually with the passing of RT.

- Gaining TP -
  TP are accumulated both with the passing of RT, and when a unit attacks or is attacked.

  More powerful actions consume large amounts of MP and TP, so their use must be timed carefully.

{span 18 5651 0d 80}  Magic-using classes such as Wizards must first make the following preparations to use spells:

- Learning Spells -
  To learn a spell you must first obtain the corresponding arcana. When you have an arcana in your possession, the spell contained within can be learned by selecting Magic under the Party command. Spells can also be learned by using arcana as items during battle.

- Command Skills -
  To use a spell you have learned, you must also learn the command skill for the spell's elemental school. Once a command skill has been learned, it must be assigned before it can be used in battle. After a skill is assigned, it will appear under the Act command.

Example: Casting Heal
1. Obtain the Grimoire Vitalite.

2. Select Learn under Magic from the Party screen, and then select Grimoire Vitalite. The unit will learn the Heal spell.

3. Select Learn under Skills from the Party screen, and learn the Divine Magic command skill.

4. Select Assign under Skills from the Party screen, and assign the Divine Magic command skill.

{span 1a 2c48 09 20}  Consumables such as mend leaf and magic leaf can be used with the Inventory command. All units use consumables from the party's shared inventory.

- Potent Consumables -
  The Field Alchemy support skill is required to use more potent consumables. There are four levels of Field Alchemy, with higher levels granting mastery over a wider range of consumables. You can view the skills required for each from the Inventory command from the Party screen.

{span 18 7856 03 90}  Some of the more common debuffs include petrify, poison, stun, sleep, and charm.

- Petrify -
  Petrified units are turned to stone, leaving them powerless to act. Weapon attacks against them will always hit, but the damage done will be greatly reduced. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain number of attack turns.

- Poison -
  Poisoned units will take damage for a set number of turns. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain amount of RT has passed.

- Stun -
  Stunned units have a certain chance of losing the ability to act. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade after a certain number of attack turns.

- Sleep -
  Sleeping units remain stationary and their avoidance of weapon-based attacks is reduced to 0%. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade when the unit takes damage or after a certain number of attack turns.

- Charm -
  Charmed units are temporarily confused and attack their allies. The debuff can be removed using magic or items, and will also fade when the unit takes damage or after a certain number of attack turns.

  There are many other debuffs besides those listed here. When a unit is affected by a debuff, you can view details about it using the Condition command.

{span 16 5c4b 25 50}  Attacks using weapons or magic are influenced by attack type, element, and race, and each piece of armor has corresponding resistances to these. If a unit is wearing armor highly resistant to a certain attack, the damage taken is reduced.

- Attack Types -
  The three attack types are CRUSHING, PIERCING, and SLASHING, and each has a corresponding resistance.

- Elements -
  The eight elements are AIR, EARTH, LIGHTNING, WATER, FIRE, ICE, LIGHT, and DARK, and each has a corresponding resistance.

- Races -
  The nine races are HUMAN, BEAST, REPTILE, DRAGON, DIVINE, UMBRA, FAERIE, PHANTOM, and GOLEM. Some races are more or less resistant to certain spells and weapons.

{span 12 c047 01 18}  Terrain information for the selected tile is displayed on the battlefield.
  The left value indicates the melee accuracy modifier and the right value the ranged accuracy modifier. Attacking from a position with high values for the attack type used increases the chance of hitting.
  Some classes such as the Octopus receive greater bonuses on certain terrain than other classes.

{span 1a b24f 26 50}  Experience points and skill points are calculated for the entire battle party and then distributed according to a number of rules.

- Experience Points -
  The experience point total is made up of the base value for the battle and the points added when enemy units are defeated. This number is then distributed based on the classes of the surviving party members. Classes with the greatest number of surviving units receive more experience points.

- Skill Points -
  Skill points are acquired through the actions taken by your units during battle, and then added to the battle party's skill point pool. The points in the pool are distributed evenly among surviving units once the battle is over.

- Zombies -
  Be wary if any of your surviving units are zombies. Units with this condition count towards the total for point distribution, but receive no actual experience or skill points, so their portion of the total is lost.

{span 1c 5405 3c 08}  Class levels are managed by party rather than by individual units. For example, when you reach level 7 in the Warrior class, all Warrior units in your party will become level 7. This applies to newly recruited units as well, meaning even a new recruit can immediately become a level 7 Warrior in this example.

{span 14 0648 18 50}  Each unit can equip up to 5 items. However, items can only be equipped to certain location slots.

- Left Hand/Right Hand -
  Weapons and shields are equipped to hand slots. Two one-handed weapons can be equipped at the same time, but only one two-handed weapon can be equipped. Shields can only be equipped in the left hand.
  
- Armor -
  Two pieces of armor can be equipped, covering head, body, arms, or legs.

- Jewelry -
  A single piece of jewelry can be equipped.

{span 10 3048 01 18}  Using the Party command you can view information about each unit in your party and customize their equipment and skills.
  Select a unit from the list and press the {icon 3} button to move to the unit information screen. Here you can perform actions such as changing a unit's equipment or class.
  Press the {icon 4} button while the Unit List is displayed to switch to class list display. This makes it easy to view details such as the level of each class.

{span 1a 8653 02 88}  Skills are abilities that each unit can learn by spending the skill points they acquire. Each class has access to different skills, but some can be used by other classes once they have been learned. You can increase the number of skill slots by spending skill points, up to a maximum of 10 slots.

  The four skill types are command, support, action, and special.

- Command Skills -
  These add sub-commands that can be accessed using the Act command. Includes skills such as Divine Magic.

- Support Skills -
  Support skills take effect automatically once they are assigned. There are many kinds, such as those that change movement type or increase attack power.

- Action Skills -
  Action skills can be executed using the Skills command once they are assigned. They require TP to use.

- Special Skills -
  These include skills such as dragon breath that are only available to certain races. They appear under the Act command.

  Units can gain proficiency with certain skills when they are used in battle, raising their skill rank. You may even acquire finishing moves unique to certain weapons by raising the skill rank of your weapon skills.

{span 12 144c 2c 98}  Many features that become available as you proceed through the game can still be used after jumping to a different point in the story using the World Tarot.

- Battle -
  Chariot Tarot
  The AI command
  Optional battles

- Shops -
  Crafting
  Items for sale

- The Warren Report -
  Titles
  Music

- Notes -
  Titles earned and music unlocked are never lost when the World Tarot is used. They are still accessible in the Warren Report.
  The Wheel of Fortune command is renamed World Tarot. Anchor points appear on the time line, and can be selected and jumped to.
  Time line records will also remain, and new events will continue to be added. However, when the same event is repeated multiple times, previous records are overwritten by newer ones.

{span 14 4a4a 01 38}  The Warren Report contains details of past events, profiles of the people you've met, and news from throughout the isles.

- Recommended Viewing -
  Some events can only be seen from the report. In fact, reading the report may sometimes reveal new locations on the world map. Be sure to peruse it whenever you have the chance.

- Events Past and Present -
  Talk and People contain information about current happenings in Valeria, while the Wheel of Fortune, Tidings, and Play Guide detail the history you've helped to write. Keep this in mind when viewing each category.

{span 19 5e4b 14 28 185e30313030}  You may be drawn into battle at locations on the world map you've visited before. These are known as optional battles.
  During optional battles you may face unique enemies and monsters that are seldom seen elsewhere. They're also a chance to obtain rare items. What's more, {hero} does not need to take part in optional battles, and you can even choose to retreat from them entirely.

- Two Forms of Retreat -
  You can retreat either while forming a battle party before battle, or after battle commences. If you retreat before entering battle, it does not count towards your battles fought. You can see how many battles you've fought in the Warren Report.

{span 0c 0e44 26 10}  You can craft items in shops to upgrade your current equipment and create new pieces not normally offered for sale.
  Crafting requires a recipe and the necessary ingredients and items. There is a risk that crafting may fail.

{span 18 7a05 0a 08}  Your party can contain up to 50 units. You cannot recruit new units after the maximum has been reached; you must first dismiss one or more units to make room. The guests that join you as you make your way through the story do not count toward your unit total.

{span 16 5048 13 10}  The skills of a unit with no remaining life can be transferred to another unit. This is called scavenging skills. The Scavenge Skills command is only available when a deceased unit is selected on the party screen.
  A silver oberyth is needed to scavenge skills. Upon selecting a recipient, all skills learned by the deceased unit will be transferred. You cannot scavenge skills from a unit that has not learned any skills. These units can only be dismissed.

{span 0e c24e 3b 98}  The {icon 1} button and directional buttons can be used in combination in a number of ways.

- Menu Screens -
  When viewing a list such as those found on the Party screen or in the Warren Report, press the {icon 1} button + {icon 18} to move up or down a page.
  You can also press the {icon 1} button + {icon 19} to cycle through the various weapon and spell information screens.

- The World Map -
  Press the {icon 1} button + {icon 18} to zoom in and out.

- The Battlefield -
  Press the {icon 1} button + {icon 18} to zoom in and out.
  Press the {icon 1} button + {icon 19} to switch to an overhead view. {icon 8} and {icon 7} rotate the view in different directions.

- Dialogue -
  When messages take up more than a single page, press the {icon 1} button + {icon 5} to return to a previous page.

- Wheel of Fortune -
  Press the {icon 1} button + {icon 18} to zoom in and out.
  On the time line, press the {icon 1} button + {icon 7} to jump to the start of the next chapter, and the {icon 1} button + {icon 8} to jump to the start of the previous chapter.
{span 0e b043 0f 08}  Press the {icon 12} button + the {icon 10} button to take a screenshot and save it to the storage media. You can view your screenshots from the System Menu.

{span 16 5647 3f 10}  The accuracy of attacks is affected by the facing of the target. Attacks from the side are more accurate than those from the front, and attacks from the rear are more accurate than those from the side.
  When targeted by an attack, you have better avoidance from the side than from the rear, and better avoidance from the front than from the side. Prepare for potential enemy attacks by choosing your facing wisely at the end of each turn.

{span 18 b405 10 08}  Units can use melee weapons such as swords and axes to attack enemies at higher or lower positions. Weapons with a range of 1 can reach enemies at elevations up to 2 higher and 3 lower than the attacking unit. Floating units can reach elevations 3 higher and lower.

{span 14 3249 2e 48}  Ranged weapons are classified as bow-type or crossbow-type depending on their firing arc.

- Bow-Type Weapons -
  Bow-type weapons fire projectiles in an arc. Thrown stones are included in this category.

- Crossbow-Type Weapons -
  Crossbow-type weapons fire projectiles in a straight line. Ninja throwing blades are included in this category.

  When making a ranged attack from high ground, you can target units outside the normal weapon range. Conversely, when making a ranged attack from low ground, even targets within range can be difficult to hit.

{span 12 ee49 12 18}  Weapon skill ranks can be raised by assigning a weapon skill and attacking with the corresponding weapon. Once the skill rank is high enough, the unit can learn finishing moves unique to that type of weapon.
  Finishing moves require TP to use. They can only be used when the corresponding weapon is equipped. You can view the finishing moves a unit has learned from the Party Menu and during battle.
  Each weapon type has several finishing moves. Higher weapon skill ranks allow access to more powerful finishing moves.

{span 16 d451 36 48}  Sometimes an attack causes the target to be moved back one tile. This is called knockback. Knockbacks can occur due to critical hits, as well as skills and specific weapon attacks.
  There are certain situations in which knockback is impossible. In general, knockback moves the target back one tile, but this does not occur if the tile in question contains an obstacle or another unit, or if it is at a higher elevation than the starting tile.

- Causing Knockback -
  It is difficult to make critical hits consistently. Attacking with a shield is a more reliable method. Shields usually have a higher chance of causing knockback. There are also skills that raise the chance of successfully knocking a target back.

- Using Knockback -
  If an enemy is knocked down from a certain height, it will take additional damage from the fall. The damage increases with elevation and the weight of the unit.
  Knocking enemies into chasms or off walls can also cause that unit to lose a life and be removed from the battlefield. However, flying units are not affected by this.

{span 14 384c 15 48}  Support skills take effect automatically once they are assigned.

- Rampart Aura -
  This skill limits the movement of enemy units. A yellow line encircles tiles surrounding units with this skill assigned. Walking units entering this area are forced to stop regardless of whether they have movement left.

- Counterattack -
  This skill triggers a counterattack following an attack by an enemy unit. Units with this skill assigned will counterattack when targeted by a melee attack as long as their equipped weapon has the necessary range.

  There are many other support skills, such as those that change movement type or increase attack. Choose skills that complement a unit's class and the layout of the battlefield.

{span 1c 5005 36 08}  Weather can affect the accuracy of attacks and the cost of movement on the battlefield. The worse the weather, the lower attack accuracy will be. The cost of moving through difficult terrain such as swamps also increases in rainy or snowy weather. This penalty further increases with heavy rain or snow.

{span 0e 6e49 25 50}  Press the {icon 12} button during battle to open the System Menu and view information about the battlefield.

- Weather -
  Weather changes between five levels over time. When the weather worsens, it may rain or snow depending on the battlefield.

- Element -
  Each battlefield has an elemental affinity that can be altered by spells and skills. The battlefield's element affects the strength of spells and skills. 

- Condition -
  This indicates any special condition affecting the battlefield. The condition of the battlefield can be altered by skills.

{span 10 c245 36 10}  You may discover hidden items when your units move to certain parts of the battlefield. These items are called buried treasure.
  Buried treasure can be found in a wide variety of locations, and sometimes requires that grass or snow be burned away to reveal the earth beneath before it can be discovered.

{span 16 5e04 34 08}  You can only hold up to 99 of each item. If you obtain more of an item you already carry the maximum of during battle, the excess will be converted to goth. Note that you'll receive less than you would if you had sold the items in a shop.

{span 10 5a4d 39 68}  You can sometimes befriend enemy units by using skills such as Recruit, Coax, and Subdue during battle. The chance of success is affected by range, loyalty, and HP.

- Range -
  You should try to get as close as possible to units you want to recruit. They will often ignore you if you merely shout at them from afar.

- Loyalty -
  Check the loyalty of the enemy unit. Units with lower loyalty are easier to recruit. You can judge the loyalty of a unit from the select help text when its name is selected.

- HP -
  Try to reduce the HP of the enemy unit as much as possible to increase your chances of success. One tenth their maximum HP is a good target.

- Failed Recruitment -
  Each time you fail at recruiting, the target's loyalty increases, making the next attempt more difficult. Try to make the first time count.

{span 10 2447 09 18}  Sometimes defeated enemies will leave behind a bag of loot or tarot card.
  Tarot cards can be collected by ending a unit's turn on the tile containing the tarot card. The unit's stats will increase, with different cards affecting different stats.
  Bags of loot are collected in the same way. If a pouch contains an arcana, you can also learn the spell it contains after picking it up.

{span 14 084c 1a 50}  When battle ends, you will receive experience points, skill points, and the spoils of war. Units may also join or leave your party.

- Collecting Items -
  Bags of loot remaining on the battlefield are collected and the items inside added to your inventory. However, tarot cards are not recovered.

- Units Joining the Party -
  Enemy units you successfully recruit can be added to your party after the battle is over. If you already have the maximum number of units, you must either turn the new unit away or dismiss another unit first.

- Units Leaving the Party -
  If the loyalty of your units falls too low, they will leave after the battle is over. Take note if any of your units voice complaints at the end of a fight.

{span 10 f047 3d 18}  Units have loyalty to their respective leaders. Though this value is not listed as a stat, it can be guessed from the select help message that appears when their name is selected.
  Units with low loyalty may leave your party at the end of a battle. The loyalty of a unit drops when you take actions they do not support, such as defeating enemies of their own clan.
  Take note if any of your units voice complaints at the end of a fight.

{span 14 d247 3e 10}  You can set your units to AI control to have them act for themselves during battle. There are six AI settings available, including Melee, which sets a unit to fight aggressively, and Vanguard, which sets a unit to hold the front line.
  When you want to restore manual control, select Manual from the AI menu. When the attack turns of AI units run consecutively, you can interrupt their actions and issue commands by pressing the {icon 4} button.

{span 16 2204 2f 08}  Your units can step on other monster units in your party during battle. All monster units have an elevation of 3. You can use this to your advantage by bridging a gap 3 steps high and 2 tiles wide by positioning a monster unit below.

{span 14 2446 09 10}  Skeletons, ghosts, and zombie units are stilled when their HP reaches 0. Stilled units appear identical to incapacitated units, but when the number above their head reaches 0, they reanimate and rejoin the battle.
  Undead can be hard to defeat, but certain spells and skills can destroy them while in this weakened state.

{span 16 4404 2f 08}  Some obstacles on the battlefield can be destroyed. When these obstacles are selected, they display an HP value like enemy units. There is not always a need to destroy them, but it can serve to give you a tactical advantage at times.

  Krysaro has long been a center of worship for followers of Vasque, and it is but a matter of time before it returns to its former glory.

{span 12 3845 35 10}  Opponents of the Galgastani regime in Coritanae held a large rally upon hearing that Almorica Castle had fallen.
  Many have been secretly critical of Hierophant Balbatos, and now this discontent has come to the fore. The Hierophant is responding with force, slaying all those who speak out against him.

{span 18 fe05 16 08}  Partisans thought to be behind the attack of a procession in Heim on the first of Godscale have now been apprehended. They are believed to be members of the Liberation Front, a group of Bakram militants loyal to the late King Dorgalua. We now await further announcements.

{span 0e 7a45 1b 10}  Nybeth Obdilord, a well-known practitioner of the art of necromancy and the Galgastani consul to Almorica, has gone missing.
  He has not been heard from since the fall of Almorica Castle, and is likely a prisoner of the Walister Resistance. There is grave fear for his safety.

{span 16 9a47 1a 10}  The Liberation Front is made up of Bakram partisans loyal to the late King Dorgalua. Though they promote equality regardless of ethnicity or religious beliefs, their violent tactics have been called into question following a number of civilian deaths.
  Front leader Cerya Phoraena vehemently denies any part in these killings. She states this is merely propaganda targeted at discrediting their cause.

{span 0e 4645 07 10}  A group of Resistance forces have broken through Galgastani lines at Rhime. Sir Leonar of the Knights of Almorica is thought to be among them.
  Leonar is a senior member of the Resistance, and it is rumored he was sent as envoy to seek aid from the Bakram.

{span 16 4046 34 10}  Duke Ronwey has decreed that the Phorampa Wildwood, which has long been neglected due to the war, is to be opened to hunters. Though hunting will first be limited to the southern tracts bordering Tynemouth, other areas are to follow.
  The Walister are growing in power, but they yet lack funds. It is thought they seek to profit from Phorampa's bountiful reserves.

{span 18 b848 05 10}  A massacre has taken place at Balmamusa. There are no survivors. Balmamusa was set aside for the Walister by the Kingdom of Galgastani, and all those who perished were of Walister blood. Women and children were spared no mercy as the town was engulfed in flames.
  The killings are thought to be an act of retribution by the Galgastani for the recapture of Almorica Castle by the Resistance. Hierophant Balbatos maintains he is not responsible.

{span 1e 2c06 0d 08}  Hearing of the massacre at Balmamusa, factions within the Galgastani camp have risen up against their leaders. They sought to oust the Hierophant, but army forces have crushed the rebellion with a savage display of force. Many are deserting the army or seeking to incite a coup d'état, and the chain of command is in tatters.

{span 1a fc05 29 08}  The Walister Resistance has placed a bounty on the head of the young Hero of Golyat who recaptured Almorica Castle. They have named him as the one responsible for the massacre at Balmamusa. He has thus far evaded pursuit, and is now in hiding. The bounty stands at a staggering 30,000 goth.

{span 1c 6205 38 08}  Reports indicate that forces of the Walister Resistance led by Duke Ronwey are massing in the Psonji Weald near Coritanae Keep. Galgastani now make up about half the Resistance army, and the battle lines are no longer as clearly drawn as in the past. It seems a final push will be made in the coming days.

{span 1a 2605 1a 08}  The Walister Resistance has captured Coritanae Keep, the Galgastani seat of power. The keep was taken with little resistance, making the battle of the Psonji Weald the last major engagement of the war. Galgastani leader Hierophant Balbatos was executed the following morning.

{span 1a 5605 1c 08}  Bakram forces launched a new offensive on Rhime mere days after the downfall of the Kingdom of Galgastan. They now battle soldiers of the Walister Resistance garrisoned there, and both sides have suffered heavy losses. Refugees from Rhime are streaming into the Phidoch region.

{span 1c 6805 3a 08}  Another tragedy reminiscent of the massacre at Balmamusa has occurred. A great many of the townspeople of Rhime have fallen victim to the Bakram invasion. At least 5,000 are believed dead, and bodies litter the streets. With skirmishes still taking place, as yet nothing can be done to put the dead to rest.

{span 18 b848 05 10}  A massacre has taken place at Balmamusa. There are no survivors. Balmamusa was set aside for the Walister by the Kingdom of Galgastani, and all those who perished were of Walister blood. Women and children were spared no mercy as the town was engulfed in flames.
  The killings are thought to be an act of retribution by the Galgastani for the recapture of Almorica Castle by the Resistance. Hierophant Balbatos maintains he is not responsible.

{span 1c 9a05 3d 08}  It is now rumored Duke Ronwey had a hand in the massacre that took place in Balmamusa. Some suggest the killings were a ploy to cause internal strife in Galgastan. The Duke denies these rumors. Meanwhile, opponents of the Hierophant in Galgastan are still wary of laying the blame for the massacre on Balbatos.

{span 1a 4e05 1d 08}  Reports indicate that the Galgastani forces led by Hierophant Balbatos are massing in the Psonji Weald near Coritanae Keep. With the Resistance growing in numbers and Galgastani opponents of the war becoming more vocal, it is thought Galgastani forces will make their move soon.

{span 1c d406 03 08}  Curious posters have been sighted in Rhime in recent days. They say simply, "The nobility must be overthrown." They are the work of the New Walister Alliance, who seek self-governance for their people. Support for this new faction is growing fast among the poorer classes, and authorities seek to unmask its leader.

{span 1e 9406 17 08}  A major battle has been fought between Galgastani and Walister forces at the Psonji Weald. Both sides incurred heavy losses in fighting that raged for more than a day, but the Galgastani emerged victorious. The Resistance were unfamiliar with the lay of the land, and the Galgastani clinched victory upon the arrival of reinforcements.

{span 1c 6805 3a 08}  Another tragedy reminiscent of the massacre at Balmamusa has occurred. A great many of the townspeople of Rhime have fallen victim to the Bakram invasion. At least 5,000 are believed dead, and bodies litter the streets. With skirmishes still taking place, as yet nothing can be done to put the dead to rest.

{span 18 fc05 17 08}  The Bakram had been quiet of late, but have now resumed their offensive with a surprise attack on Rhime. They battle soldiers of the Walister Resistance garrisoned there, and both sides have suffered heavy losses. Refugees from Rhime are streaming into the Phidoch region.

{span 16 e047 19 10}  Ravness Loxaerion, sought by the Resistance for her involvement in the massacre at Balmamusa, has been captured at Port Asyton in the Kingdom of Galgastan.
  She led Resistance forces in a number of past battles, and is a bitter enemy of Galgastan. The Resistance requested she be handed over to them, but the Galgastani camp refused. She is to be escorted to Coritanae Keep where she faces execution.

{span 16 6404 30 08}  Duke Ronwey of the Walister Resistance has met with Galgastani leaders to negotiate the dissolution of the army and the formal handover of Coritanae. This signals the end of the Kingdom of Galgastan established by Hierophant Balbatos.

{span 14 8404 1d 08}  Former Galgastani soldiers are flocking to the Walister Resistance. Many of them long to end the war that has stretched on for more than two years, and they are eager to prove their mettle against the Bakram armies.

{span 1e cc06 1a 08}  A large number of refugees fled Rhime for neighboring regions when the Bakram invaded. Those who had taken up in Phidoch have started to make their way home. The Bakram claim the restoral of public order in Rhime is to thank for this, but refugees state their poor treatment at the hands of the people of Phidoch has forced them to leave.

{span 0e a045 0e 10}  Mount Weobry in the Burnham Massif has erupted for the first time in six score years. The blast shook the land for miles, but tremors have now subsided.
  Though the Valerian Isles are volcanic, Mount Hedon on Banhamuba was the only known active volcano until now.

{span 12 e647 08 10}  Almorica Castle has been attacked by remnants of the Galgastani army. The Resistance suffered few losses, but were caught off guard by the late-night assault, and the castle fell.
  Elite Galgastani forces were made up of Balbatos loyalists, and most have continued to fight. Though Coritanae has been annexed, it will be some time before the Resistance wins the hearts of its people.

{span 1b 7445 22 08 1a7430313030}  Vyce Bozeck, once a top member of the Resistance, now has a bounty of 50,000 goth on his head. This is the largest in recorded history. Vyce is accused of plotting to kill Duke Ronwey, and has not been seen for over a month. He was the childhood friend of {hero} Pavel, the Hero of Golyat.

{span 0a e244 0d 18}  The bounty for Vyce Bozeck, wanted for plotting the assassination of Duke Ronwey, now stands at 60,000 goth.
 This is a princely sum, and bounty hunters now scour the lands for a chance at the purse.

{span 1e c006 12 08}  There have been many strange sightings at Port Asyton, gateway to the war-torn Coritanae lands. Bodies have been robbed from its cemetery, and residents thought dead have been seen on the streets. Resistance forces were dispatched to investigate, but have not been heard from since. The townspeople now avoid going out after dusk.

{span 1a ce05 26 08}  Remnants of the Galgastani army have captured Coritanae Keep from the Walister Resistance. The assault was led by High Commander Xaebos, a close aid of the late Hierophant Balbatos. He played a key role in the blood war, and is wanted for crimes committed against the peoples of Valeria.

{span 1e 4e06 11 08}  Remnants of the Galgastani army currently holed up in Coritanae Keep are now calling for fellow survivors to return to their posts. It is not known how many former soldiers have answered the call. The Galgastani also plan to execute several Walister Resistance soldiers in the days to come, including wanted criminal Vyce Bozeck.

{span 20 0c06 17 08}  Resistance forces have once again captured Coritanae Keep. High Commander Xaebos was slain in the battle. The Galgastani stragglers who had continued fighting the Resistance are now no more. Peace has returned to Coritanae at last. The whereabouts of former Resistance soldier Vyce Bozeck who had been held at the castle are not known.

  All are curious at what Pavel's next move may be.

{span 1a 3805 1d 08}  Brigantys Castle has been captured by remnants of the Galgastani army. High Commander Xaebos leads the survivors, and is urging other Galgastani soldiers to regroup, but few have answered the call. It is thought the Walister Resistance will move to recapture the castle quickly.

{span 13 dc45 25 10 13dc30313030 08de30313030}  Brigantys Castle has been liberated by the Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel. High Commander Xaebos was slain in the battle. The Galgastani stragglers who had continued fighting the Resistance are now no more.
  It is not known why {hero} Pavel would aid the Resistance, who have put a price on his head.

{span 13 b644 35 10 12b630313030}  Resistance forces have captured Coritanae Keep in {hero} Pavel's absence. Duke Ronwey has stated that Pavel will be shown no mercy, despite appearances that he may be seeking to rejoin the Resistance.
  It seems that peace still eludes Coritanae.

{span 18 3247 0b 10}  A storm is raging off the coast of Oedlark. The waters around the island are known for their fickle currents, and the storm has only made these worse. The approach to the undersea caverns called the Pirate's Graveyard is currently too treacherous to navigate.
  Though thought to be a temporary anomaly, pirates in these parts whisper that the storm was called by a creature of the deep.

{span 1b 1e4a 19 18 173430323030 081230313030}  King {hero} announced his intention to establish a provisional government at Heim. King {hero} is set to rule, having the backing of both Resistance leaders and the general populace. The king's close associates will be part of the new administration.
  He has also announced the Resistance is to be dissolved. With war at an end and the Dark Knights destroyed, the Resistance no longer serves a purpose. Its soldiers will join the king's guard or be assigned other posts to ensure they are rewarded for the service they have given.
  Heim Castle is bustling with the preparations for King {hero}'s coronation.

{span 1b da49 36 10 184030313030}  With the Heim Conflict that erupted following the death of King Dorgalua at an end, King Tristan of the Kingdom of New Xenobia pledged to support King {hero} in restoring the isles to their former glory. It is rumored that his envoys have already been sent to Heim.
  The Holy Lodissian Empire has made no comment thus far. With the collapse of the Bakram-Valerian Kingdom they had lent aid to through a secret treaty, they surely cannot remain silent for much longer. Interestingly, it seems the destruction of the Dark Knights has yet to be announced in Lodis.

{span 15 464a 0d 20 10c230313030}  Though the war in Valeria is at an end, bands of armed militia still roam the lands. The Tigers of Burnham is one such group. Based in the Burnham Highlands, they have been implicated in a number of assassinations.

 They recently claimed that King {hero} drove Princess Versalia to her grave to usurp her power, and stated their intention to capture Heim from the Resistance to restore rightful order.
  Though they fight under the banner of justice for all Valerians, former Bakram and Galgastani soldiers are joining their ranks in droves, and doubts have been cast on their motives.

{span 28 e64a 36 10}  Valeria has a thriving sea trade, and many fortresses have been built to protect its ports from enemies. During King Dorgalua's reign soldiers of the Kingdom of Valeria were garrisoned at each fortress, but since the kingdom's downfall they have been manned sporadically at best. This has led to an increase in pirates, bandits, and army stragglers capturing the fortresses for their own use. Gecho Fortress on Beneceunga fell into pirate hands just the other day.
  As Gecho is south of the prominent trading port of Grimsby, merchants there are anxious to see the pirates routed from the fortress as soon as possible.

{span 18 9c05 10 08}  Rumor has it that remnants of the Galgastani army are gathering at Lhazan Fortress, site of the recent Bakram massacre of Vasque faithful. The Galgastani soldiers' plans are not known, but they could seek to use the fortress as a stronghold to fight the Resistance.

  Though the Valerian Isles are volcanic, Mount Hedon on Banhamuba was the only known active volcano until now.

{span 1a 4805 1e 08}  Duke Ronwey was slain at Almorica Castle while Resistance and Bakram forces battled at Rhime. A close ally, Sir Leonar, was behind the killing. Since the massacre at Balmamusa there had been growing concern about the Duke's ability to lead, and this ultimately led to his demise.

{span 1b 9a45 26 08 1a9a30323030}  A new leader of the Walister Resistance has emerged following the Duke's death. The Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel, who acted swiftly to put down Leonar's rebellion, now heads the Resistance. {hero} has also allied with the New Walister Alliance, which enjoys a great deal of support among the people.

{span 1c 2005 35 08}  Reports indicate that the Galgastani forces led by Hierophant Balbatos are massing in the Psonji Weald south of Coritanae Keep. They are likely to strike while the Resistance is preoccupied with the Bakram invasion of Rhime and the change of leadership following Sir Leonar's assassination of the Duke.

{span 1d 0a45 32 08 1c0a30313030}  The Galgastani seat of power, Coritanae Keep, has fallen. It seems Resistance soldiers battling the Galgastani at the Psonji Weald were merely decoys, as another force led by the Hero of Golyat, {hero} Pavel, assailed the undermanned keep. Galgastani leader Hierophant Balbatos was killed in the fighting.

{span 20 c806 33 08}  Many Galgastani soldiers surrendered to the Walister Resistance following the death of Hierophant Balbatos. The Resistance took control of major cities such as Port Asyton and the mining town of Balmamusa. As the Galgastani forces sent to the Psonji Weald remain at large, surrendering soldiers are held as prisoners of war to prevent them joining the fray again.

He played a key role in the blood war, and is wanted for crimes committed against the peoples of Valeria. He has also taken Resistance officer Vyce Bozeck prisoner.

{span 14 8404 1d 08}  Former Galgastani soldiers are flocking to the Walister Resistance. Many of them long to end the war that has stretched on for more than two years, and they are eager to prove their mettle against the Bakram armies.

{span 1a 8a05 21 08}  Almorica Castle has been liberated by Resistance forces. High Commander Xaebos was slain in the battle. The Galgastani stragglers who had continued fighting the Resistance are now no more. This signals the end of the Kingdom of Galgastan established by the late Hierophant Balbatos.

{span 18 ac48 1d 10}  The Lord of Coritanae, premier of the Kingdom of Galgastan, has gone missing. Hierophant Balbatos has declared the Lord kidnapped by those seeking to exploit his position. The search is ongoing.
  No strangers were sighted in the vicinity of the Lord's quarters, nor have any traces of an intruder been found, so authorities believe it the work of an insider. Denizens of the keep fear greatly for their Lord's safety, and worry at reports of the Resistance's advance.

{span 1a 8e4f 31 20}  The Bay of Gobanda is known for the thick fog that hangs over its waters. It was recently discovered that an immense tower lies hidden within the fog.
  Scholars from the Royal Academy say it once stood in the ancient city of San Bronsa, which was destroyed in Dorgalua's great war. The Bay of Gobanda was formed when magic wielded by King Rodrick of Brigantys shattered the lands in the last days of the war, also destroying San Bronsa.
  Scholars had studied the tower before the great war, but it is still not known when it was built, or by whom. It is said the Hanging Gardens built by King Dorgalua were inspired by the tower of San Bronsa.
  As news of the tower's discovery spreads there is concern it will be looted by thieves, and the Resistance is considering sending an exploratory party there. There have been further reports of a large island floating in the sky above the bay, but nothing more is known at this point.

{span 27 5a56 37 28 0d7630313030 265a30323030}  Many strange rumors have been circulating of late. People thought dead have been seen walking about, and the same person sighted in two places at once. Normally little stock would be put into such rumors, but there is much talk about these incidents among scholars and mages. Some believe them the work of the Apocrypha, others attribute them to some arcane art brought from Lodis.
  A common thread is found throughout these reports. The young hero of the Resistance, {hero}, is always mentioned by witnesses.
  {hero} is famed as a warrior and tactician, but few know of his penchant for collecting tarot cards. He is apparently particularly fond of the Wheel of Fortune card. It is not clear how this relates to the current rumors, but the Wheel of Fortune card has long been a symbol of regret and atonement in Valeria. It would not be beyond reason for {hero} himself to be struggling with such feelings, having experienced war at such a young age.
  What would one do if the power to bend time fell into our hands? One could repeat an exercise, knowing the best solution in advance. Or learn a lover plans to leave you before they speak a word. And who would not go back to save the lives of fallen comrades?
  However, one thing must be kept in mind: A different past is no guarantee of a happier future. Changing what has happened may in fact have no effect at all on the here and the now.

{span 18 c205 14 08}  The songstress Iuria has won great fame for her talents, but since her arrival death seems to stalk the sick and weak in Omish. The requiems she sings when the dead are laid to rest may bring tears with their beauty, but some believe her to be the dreaded Wicce Sirene.

{span 1c 7e05 35 08}  A stone tablet found at the Palace of the Dead on Exeter this month past has been deciphered. Scholars at the Royal Academy announced the tablet to contain the message, "A sealed door lies three floors below ground." This discovery already appears to be common knowledge among treasure-hunting thieves.

{span 1e c806 1e 08}  In the ancient Bolsenian era, the Dragon Lords built a civilization that flourished across Xytegenia and the surrounding isles. They are said to be the source of the magic practiced today, but much of this knowledge perished with them. On rare occasions arcana from this era are discovered at ancient ruins, and these are highly sought after.
